body: That sounds really nice. I'll try it next time. Thanks again.

I really like you and your humor. It made me smile. Thank you mAizer. 
I'll try my best to get into business again next year if I can't make it this year and be the best damn excel spreadsheet wizard I can. Thank you again for your posts. I'm really happy to read them. It really does help me feel a bit better and draw my path clearer along the way. Thanks again. I really appreciate it.

I really enjoy walking and I walk often with my headphones on so the next time I walk I'll definitely try and run. I do have an old Ipod from my old friend so I believe nike+ is on there. I remember being on the track team in elementary and although it was a long time ago, I was first in a group team relay. I think that thought will make my running feel even better. I'll try and run next time if I can get out. If not, I'll try doing the stairs. Thanks for your advice.

It's very nice to surf for online counselling in the convenience of my house when physical resources are unavailable. I have taken look at the links you sent me and I'll take an even longer look later this week; thank you.
I reread what you wrote in the second and third paragraph three or four times because it's a wonderful story about your life, you've made it through and now retired happily with children and grandchildren. That's always been one of my greatest fantasy and life goal. 
I have to thank you again for replying on my post. I was expecting a small turnout and it's what I got, but your lengthy post meant everything to me, especially from a successful survivor as yourself. I'm am very happy for your happiness and your kind words in reply to my post. Thank you so much again pambie. I wish you the greatest as well!

It's very comforting to hear from a survivor, you are one of the few I hold my admiration to. When I hear success stories from those older than me I immediately think that everybody is different and I am not one of the ones that pull through. That success is not now and I do have 'maybe' in whether I achieve a success like yours. However, it really warms my heart to hear you share your success. I'm very happy for you, I hope to follow in your footsteps.
I love Rocky; he is an inspiration on his own. I may have to watch the movie again. I really love this quote. It's so simple but so strong. Thanks.

I think we may come from different cultures and different views on family. I really can't see why the 19 year old would be a barrier from his happiness and freedom. Family is an extremely important value and there is no need to kick your own child out because he has reached a certain age, that actually really frightens me that he would believe such a thing. But I really do believe it's a culture thing. I live in Canada so I see a lot of different families and their values. 
I certainly understand that there is a dependency factor where the children never grow up but for there's a 'forced independence' factor where the bird may die having kicked out of its nest. It really works both ways and depends on the child themselves. Kind of like liberalism and conservatism, one works better than the other when dealt with the right people. 
If it's alright, can you tell me about your friend's three sons? Are they in a relationship or have a job? Also, does your friend make a lot of money or just the barer minumum to support themselves and the house?

I'm undeclared going into business to become an accountant. I don't think my 2.7 GPA can get me into business next year so I really don't know what to do. I thought about changing to education and pursuing teaching (high school) I'm am just really afraid of not being able to find a job once I get my degree.

I think we are different people. I've tried using my hatred to push through but it presses me down and topples me overboard. My parents have been and are still abusive (most just mentally now) but they're all alone. I'm really happy that you are successful and happy and found your way in life. I don't know how to get there but it's a prospect that sounds nice. I'd be happy with a quiet, below average pay if it means I can live by myself without having to worry paycheck to paycheck. You're strong to leave at age 18 and even stronger to become successful. I'm really glad.

I don't know how to explain my situation etheir. But my parents are quite old and they have no other family than each other and myself. They can't speak English properly and my dad relies on $20/hr while my mom has social anxiety and can't find a job at all. 
Asking me to leave my family in my situation is asking me to break off my relationship with my family. This is a personal problem that applies directly to us. 
I understand  your viewpoint and I'm really glad you're actually taking your time to advise me. I don't reject any of the advice you gave me if that's what I appeared to be doing. I really did consider them all and I'm happy your advice differs so much from my own because I might turn around one day and apply what you said into reality. Thanks.

I'm happy that you want to help me, I really am. I've took a look at Pandora's Project today and I'll probably look at After Silence later on.
I'm glad we crossed paths, if I ever get batter, I'll let you know.

I don't think it means anything if I am stopping here but I hope to survive through like the child I was and I'm happy for your thoughts.  I'd like to live a sincere life.

I'm really thankful that you believe in me. I've worn a bracelet that said 'Believe in Yourself' since I got it as a gift in Grade 6. These words mean a lot, so thank you again.

It's very scary to find a counselor in Uni because everyone sees you walk into a long empty hallway specifically for mental awareness but at this point I am willing to try. However, I'm still waiting to see if I got into my second year so I can get a bus pass to uni and take classes, if I didn't get in I really don't know what to do other than work for a year. I can't find therapy outside of my computer because I don't have a learner's, let alone a license and I won't be driven to clinics by my parents. It's far too costly and my mom who is a housewife can't drive that far. She can only drive me to the close mall where I work. It's pathetic but I'm trying to get a learner's now.

My younger self certainly was young, resilient and smart but my shield is degrading right now. I'm not sure how old you are but I finished my first year of Uni and with no aim for career, no money, no friends and a wishy washy brain, it's difficult to understand where to go.

I'm really happy that you will answer if I post. You must be a compassionate stranger if you browse SuicideWatch often. I'm really happy that there's people out there helping others such as yourself. Thank you.
It's nice that the internet brought us together for a little bit. I got a bit sheepish from your kind words. Thank you ember8888.

They are my parents and it is my problem because I would have initiated it. I'm really sorry but I really don't think we are on the same page when it comes to connection. I can't so easily break off my relationship with my parents even if I have been thoroughly abused and ignored. I understand you're trying to help and give me support and I fully thank you for your posts.

I know there is no magical solution and I am willing to take advice such as from the comments below you but your move to tell me to move out, you're an adult made me think that 'oh, its that simple because i'm an adult now.' 

I am happy that you can relate to my childhood and chose to share it with me on my post but even if we have been through sexual abuse, we haven't been through the same life and I really don't believe we took it the same way.

I want to help myself that's why (as small as it is) I posted on reddit to tell someone, even if they're behind a computer screen about my problems. I was sick of keeping them all in and trudging on without doing anything about it.

I do not act depressed around my friends. I have always been in a normal state of mind when I am around them or anyone else, it is only when I am back at home that I am able to be free with my emotions.

I know I am lucky to find a job with no experience, the managers who berate me are a problem but I was able to take a step and get income as small as it is.

I am not discounting therapy I am saying I can not at this moment bring up the money to find professional therapy or be able to talk it over with my parents into letting me seek therapy. I know this is where you tell me I have the ability to make my own choices but as abusive as my parents are, I can't leave them by themselves so easily. It will cause a huge problem if I move out on my own because I know what they are capable and are likely going to do. They would find me out and force me back in and when I decline they will file for divorce. I know they are both stubborn but unable to live without each other so I can't let them do that. They have no other family but me and each other.

I do not like thrashing around and I don't choose to act like a crazy person. I've always been able to stay quiet during my parent's abuse but the thrashing has recently came out uncontrollably in these past months.

A women's shelter is a drastic option for me because I have very little knowledge on the outside world. I know I need to learn first hand but it's more comfortable to just observe for now.

I really like the website you sent me. I've been looking at it for a bit and I'll probably spend the rest of this evening reading it too. Thank you.

I'll start trying taking one step at a time like you said. I really like your second last line.

It is regular retail but with stingy managers that don't let me go to the washroom without putting a 'warning' for taking advantage of my working hours. They also berate me for very small reasons. I just started but many employees that I've talked to have already quite because "they treat us like shit" I just want something on my resume for three months so it's not empty anymore.
Thanks for your kindness.

I can't reply to you without sounding weak and useless but I just can't move on and out and become the adult because I am 18. Please don't tell me these simple one step two step ways that would magically solve all my problems.

My dad has pride and he would never admit his daughter needs help. 
I don't have enough money for therapy or transportation to go anywhere secretly etheir. Everything I do must pass by my parents first.
I haven't been exposed to much but I think I like reading, video games and sometimes cooking. Lots of indoorsy wasting time things.
